questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to visit a place with great nature. Calgary is only located an hour from the mountain which has endless activities such as hikes and skiing.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of help is offered at UofC. There are always people to ask who can help you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: you can live in many different dorms, but because KU is a little slow with its application process, many of the dorms were already taken. Although everyone from KU who wanted to live on campus was able to find a room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: the meal plan option is VERY expensive. You can easily cook in the dorms which is what I did.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Try and find a roommate on the online roommate-match-making portal. This way you have a say in who you are living with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register online. very easy and you can switch courses when you arrive as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can email many different people to help you with course registration·

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: unfortunately many of the courses had lectures at the same time and some were full before I had a chance to register. I still had mainly good courses though

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: start as early as you can since some courses fill up quick.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall there is very limited reading and if you just show up to class it is very easy to pass.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had level 200, 300, and 500. If you can I would skip the 200 courses since they are very easy (like high school material).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is quite different. they care a lot about grades and sometimes talk to you as if you are very young and inexperienced. This can be a bit annoying, but the academic level is quite easy.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
204 Global environmental change 
375 Gender and Development 
567 Introduction to programming in GIS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Gender and Development. You learn many new perspectives and the teacher is nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent most my money on renting cars to drive to the mountains for hikes. I also spent money on a season pass for Lake Louise ski resort and gear (if you dont bring it from home). I brought all my skiing gear except skis, which i bought and sold again before going home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food is more expensive. The supermarket is 1 km away so a good saving tip is to only go once a week so you aren't tempted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the Ski and Board club which was a good idea. They mainly have trips in the spring semester, but they also arrange a day trip to lake louise in November. I highly recommend this! it's loads of fun. Also they have discounted lift tickets for the resorts in Banff which is handy if you don't want to buy the season card which is expensive. It really depends on how much you hope to ski.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The gym and aquatic center are free. You can also rent squash courts which is really fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved all the active stuff

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to the mountains as much as possible! It's absolutely beautiful. You can rent a car easily through the app Turo (like danish Gomore).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I choose a Canadian roommate which helped.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, other than people are quite young. You just have to get used to it :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are very friendly and it's easy to talk to new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make the most of every weekend. It takes som planning but its definitely worth it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a different place. UofC has many international students and they are ready to help.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it too challenging. I mostly had tons of fun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Don't take school too seriously. I got A's in all my courses and didn't work too hard, although I attended all my classes and studied a day or two before a test.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
